title: Runloop incident scenarios and playroom lab notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working set of hands-on incident scenarios designed for the SDK onramp playroom. The goal is to let new integrators (and internal SDK champions) run a short lab that surfaces common runloop failure modes, exercise fallback policies, and validate telemetry / alerting. Use these as pairing exercises in onboarding, or as lab modules for bootcamps.

Audience:
- New engineers integrating Redwood SDKs into services
- DevEx engineers running onboarding sessions
- SREs and support engineers verifying observability coverage

Scope & constraints:
- Focused on the client-side runloop and immediate server fallbacks (first 10s of user request lifecycle). Does NOT simulate low-level GPU OOMs or provider network outages beyond the service edge.
- Labs assume access to the sandbox host (playroom.redwood.internal) and the local SDK dev image (rdw-sdk:dev).

Test environment quick-setup (preconditions):
1) Checkout branch: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk.git && git checkout playroom/incidents
2) Provision local sandbox: scripts/playroom/provision.sh --profile=lab201 (this creates ephemeral API keys and a joint log stream)
3) Start proxy with tracing enabled: docker-compose -f playroom/docker-compose.yml up --build tracing
4) Load sample app: node examples/chat-runloop.js --apiKey=LAB-XXX --port=3003
5) Confirm metric stream: curl http://localhost:9080/metrics | grep rdw_sdk_request

Core scenarios (fast to run, 10-25 minutes each):
A) Path jitter + transient 503s
- Setup: Use the proxy control panel to add 50-200ms variable latency and inject 10% 503 responses for /v1/generate
- Steps: Send 100 concurrent small prompts (50–80 tokens) from examples/chat-runloop.js
- Expected behaviour: SDK runloop should attempt a single immediate retry (per retry policy), emit tracing spans for retry_attempt, and fall back to cached prefix for prefix-matched requests. Application should see ~10% errors mapped to HTTP 502/504 after retry budget exhausted.
- Verification: Check traces for span tags {retry:true, retry_count:1}. Metrics: rdw_sdk_retries_total should increase, rdw_sdk_backend_errors_5xx should reflect injected 503s.
- Quick mitigation: Toggle fallback_policy to "serve-stale-cache" and re-run; errors should drop and latency improve.

B) KV cache eviction & token mismatch regression
- Setup: Begin with cache warm by sending 200 bootstrap prompts. Then lower cache size in playroom control to force eviction (LRU) and introduce a tokenization mismatch variant on one model variant.
- Steps: Re-run a suite of prompts where prefix caching is expected (same conversation).
- Expected behaviour: When cache eviction occurs, latency increases for first few requests; when combined with tokenizer change, responses show hallucinated partial context. SDK should emit a telemetry event rdw_sdk_cache_eviction with tags {evicted_keys:>10, model_variant:m1-q4}.
- Verification: Inspect application logs for "context_truncation" warnings and the telemetry stream for cache_eviction events.
- Postmortem checklist: Identify the offending model variant, roll back to previous quantization profile, expand cache, and run regression promptset.

C) Token-limit failure and graceful truncation path
- Setup: Configure a policy that prefers strict rejection on token overflow (policy: hard_fail=false), and create a long multi-turn prompt that exceeds the configured max_tokens by ~20%.
- Steps: Submit the long prompt and observe the returned error or truncated output.
- Expected behaviour: SDK should: 1) attempt to summarize the conversation (if summarization fallback enabled), 2) if summarization fails, emit a structured error with code RDW_TOKEN_LIMIT and a suggested action. Telemetry should record rdw_sdk_token_breaches_total with breach_reason:conversation_size.
- Verification: Confirm client received structured error and that the fallback_summary span exists in traces.

D) Canary model variant mismatch (rollout gating)
- Setup: Create two model variants (m1-stable, m1-canary). Route 5% of traffic to canary using smart-routing rule. Introduce a subtle prompt-output regression via a seeded prompt.
- Steps: Run the seeded prompt in a loop and monitor quality metrics and ill-formed JSON outputs.
- Expected behaviour: Observability should show quality delta for canary. The rollout should auto-halt when quality drops below threshold, and the SDK client should receive a transparent redirect to stable variant.
- Verification: Look for rollout_halted flag in product logs and rdw_rollout_quality_degradation metric.

Playroom exercises (pairing format):
- One engineer plays "integrator" (steps through SDK setup and app code), the other plays "support" (observes telemetry, toggles proxy faults, fills postmortem template).
- Exercises are timeboxed to 20 minutes each with 10 minutes retro.

Telemetry & alerting expectations (must-haves for these labs):
- Traces containing: client_request_id, sdk_version, model_variant, retry_count, latency_ms, fallback_reason
- Metrics: rdw_sdk_request_duration_seconds (p50/p95/p99 tags), rdw_sdk_retries_total, rdw_sdk_backend_errors_4xx, rdw_sdk_backend_errors_5xx, rdw_sdk_cache_eviction_total, rdw_sdk_token_breaches_total
- Events: periodic rdw_rollout_quality_degradation and rdw_playroom_lab_result (lab_id + pass/fail)

Quick smoke-check commands (for instructors):
- Check health: curl http://playroom.redwood.internal/health
- Stream traces for last 10 minutes: scripts/playroom/tail-traces.sh --last=10m --filter=rdw_sdk
- Force immediate fallback policy: scripts/playroom/flip-fallback.sh serve-stale-cache

Runbook snippets (short-term mitigations during a real incident):
- If retries spike and error budget rises: increase retry_backoff and temporarily reduce concurrency for problematic routes.
- If cache_eviction events spike: increase cache quota for the team, or disable aggressive LRU while investigating the tokenization diff.
- If rollout quality drops: revert canary, switch route to stable, create rollback PR for canary model profile.

Post-lab retro template (to paste into Confluence quickly):
- Lab id: <lab-yyyy-mm-dd-<initials>>
- Scenario: <one of A-D above>
- What happened (observed):
- Root cause hypothesis:
- Evidence (traces/metrics/logs):
- Immediate mitigation taken:
- Long-term fix & owner:
- Follow-ups (tickets):

 TODOs / follow-ups in this doc:
- Add short recorded demo videos for each scenario (screen capture + instructor audio). Owner: Jordan.
- Convert the telemetry assertions into a gating test in CI (playroom-lab-runner). Owner: Priya.
- Add a discrete lab focused on private deployment network partitions (VPC simulation). Owner: Marco.

Notes to self (choppy / for workshop prep):
- Keep scenarios modular; instructors should be able to run only one (A or B) in 10m if needed.
- Keep failure injection knobs in the dashboard simple toggles (latency %, 5xx %).
- Emphasize observable signals over code changes during initial labs — we want integrators to know "what to look for" before editing model configs.

References & links:
- Playroom control panel: https://playroom.redwood.internal
- Telemetry schema (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEX/SDK+Telemetry+Schema
- Example app: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/examples/chat-runloop.js

End of notes. Revisit after first two bootcamps to fold instructor feedback into concrete steps and sample scripts.
